back: Atoms of the same element with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.

front: Give the numbers of protons, neutrons and electrons in chlorine-35 and chlorine-37.
back: Chlorine-35: 17 p, 18 n, 17 e. Chlorine-37: 17 p, 20 n, 17 e.

front: How many neutrons are in hydrogen-1, hydrogen-2 and hydrogen-3?
back: 0, 1 and 2. Each has 1 proton and 1 electron.

front: **Supplement.** Why do isotopes of an element have the same chemical properties?
back: They have the same number of electrons and the same electronic configuration, and chemical reactions involve electrons.

front: How do isotopes of the same element differ?
back: In their numbers of neutrons, so in mass number and atomic mass; some physical properties, such as density, differ slightly.

front: What is the **relative atomic mass**, $A_r$, of an element?
back: The average mass of its isotopes, weighted by their abundances, compared with one-twelfth of the mass of a carbon-12 atom.

front: Why is the relative atomic mass of chlorine 35.5, although no atom has that mass?
back: It is a weighted average over many atoms of two isotopes (about 75% chlorine-35 and 25% chlorine-37).
